strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Reading 3:14's hand-of-YHWH construct as a fresh vision onset and cutting the unit there. Rejected because no scene change accompanies it - the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15 - so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would misclassify transit texture as a hard seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative.after: A cut at 3:13/3:14 is the live rival, weighed here face by face and not taken. Its near face, 3:14, carries two candidate drivers at once: the transport clause וְר֥וּחַ נְשָׂאַ֖תְנִי וַתִּקָּחֵ֑נִי (oshb:Ezek.3.14), which places 3:14, like the onset verse 3:12, among the transport verses the book counts (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences), and the hand-of-YHWH construct, which could be read as a fresh vision onset. Its far face, 3:13, is the sound of the creatures' wings and wheels, with no close-role formula and no parashah mark. Because a transport verb licenses a seam, the rival is not dismissed; it is held on two stated grounds. A row under three verses is held only for a complete word-event unit, and this cut would leave 3:12-13 and 3:14-15 as rows of two verses each, neither of them such a unit. And no scene change accompanies it: the same journey that begins at 3:12 continues without interruption through 3:15, so treating every occurrence of the construct as onset-grade would misclassify transit texture as a hard seam.

Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) (“I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days” (web:Ezek.3.15)); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. This is the question the division plan holds for chs 4-7, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. Named and weighed under A9: on the near face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3, and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the far face oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: in the pinned inventory no verse of ch 4 belongs to the messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event classes, the chapter's only listed members being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is absent from both the 81-verse utterance list and the 64-verse recognition family - so CUT-RULE's second limb is not met; and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side, so its first limb is not met either. A mark alone never satisfies limb (b). The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, held on those grounds, and the samekh is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates rather than for this row. The test is reworded because its earlier form omitted 4:3, the very verse the mark follows: the titled sub-onset וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ stands at 4:1 and again at 5:1, whereas bare וְאַתָּ֤ה without the title opens three interior stages - 4:3, 4:4 and 4:9 - so the text stages the siege-model, the iron pan, the two lying postures and the rationed food as one commanded act and not as separate commands (oshb:Ezek.4.1).
strongest_rejected_alternative.after: Splitting the tile sign-act (4:1-4:3) from the lying and food-rationing sign-acts (4:4-4:17) as two units. How the sign-acts of chs 4-7 divide is an open question, and the 4:3/4:4 seam is its strongest form. The mark on the verse before this cut is weighed as corroboration for the alternative: on the rival's far face the witness records a samekh after oshb:Ezek.4.3 (single-witness), and that verse closes on the sign-act colophon א֥וֹת הִ֖יא לְבֵ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.4.3), “This shall be a sign to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.4.3), standing verse-final. On the rival's near face the candidate onset oshb:Ezek.4.4 carries no formula whatever: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, no verse of ch 4 belongs to the counted messenger, utterance, recognition or word-event formula classes, the chapter's only counted device verses being the son-of-man address at 4:1 and 4:16 and the year-word non-datelines at 4:5-4:6. The colophon is not a close-role formula - oshb:Ezek.4.3 is neither an utterance-formula verse (sweep: 81 verses) nor a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses) - and the addressee is unchanged across the seam, 2ms imperatives standing to the prophet on either side. A ve'attah inside an open unit begins a sub-unit only when the addressee changes or the verse before it ends on a verse-final close-role formula; neither holds here, and a mark by itself never supplies that close. strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Holding 11:14-21 inside a single long 11:1-21 courtyard-and-oracle row, with the word-event at 11:14 disclosed only as internal texture, was weighed as an alternative reading. It was not taken because 11:14 is a strict word-event onset (not a bare transition) and the oracle's own addressee — the scattered exiles — differs from the courtyard men addressed in 11:1-13, which is enough of a class shift to justify treating it as its own formula-bounded row even while the wider vision frame stays open around it. A second rival sits inside this row, and A9/A16 weighing of it follows: a seam at 11:16/11:17. Read off the pinned section-mark record, a samekh sits on MT 11:15 and another on MT 11:16, and because each mark is keyed to the verse it stands after, both fall immediately before a verse that the pinned v2 inventory records as carrying the long messenger formula כה אמר אדני יהוה — oshb:Ezek.11.16 and oshb:Ezek.11.17, two of that class's 122 verses. CUT-RULE licenses neither seam. The addressee holds steady: the son-of-man address and the scattered exiles are named at 11:15 and nothing readdresses the oracle before 11:21. Nor does either preceding verse finish on a close-role formula — MEASURED on the pointed witness, MT 11:15 finishes לָ֥נוּ הִ֛יא נִתְּנָ֥ה הָאָ֖רֶץ לְמוֹרָשָֽׁה (oshb:Ezek.11.15) and MT 11:16 finishes בָּאֲרָצ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.11.16), while in 11:16 and in 11:17 alike the messenger formula stands at the verse's head after לכן אמר rather than at its end. No mark can satisfy that limb by itself, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21) (oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).

Neither seam is licensed as a sub-onset, since a messenger formula opens one only if the people addressed change or the verse just before it finishes on a close-role formula. A mark alone cannot stand in for that verse-final formula, so the two samekhs are disclosed for the paragraph structure they corroborate within the row, and the row rests on its strict word-event onset at 11:14 and its verse-final utterance close at 11:21 (MEASURED: נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה closes MT 11:21; oshb:Ezek.11.15, oshb:Ezek.11.21).

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). Both sides are formula-clean: a strict word-event onset and an utterance close, the tightest formula bracket in this span. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.

strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Two alternatives were weighed for MT 24:1. (1) Treating 24:1-27 as ONE unit (24:1 as the head of this collection's entire last movement, no further internal cut) — rejected because 24:15 carries its own full-form strict word-event onset (a hard seam in its own right) and a genre shift from mashal to sign-act, and both halves carry independent formula closes (24:14 and 24:27); collapsing them would also violate the granularity target. (2) Treating 24:1 as its OWN one-verse dated complex, separate from 24:2-14 — rejected because a dateline fused with a word-event in one verse is treated as a single onset that never splits, and because 24:3's dateline-day reference (verse-final words "שְׁפֹ֔ת וְגַם יְצֹ֥ק בּ֖וֹ מָֽיִם (oshb:Ezek.24.3)") ties the mashal directly to the date just given, with no seam between them. (3) Cutting at 24:8/24:9 - the alternative the Masoretic paragraph layer proposes, named and weighed here as A9 requires. What the rival's near face carries: MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness, MT 24:9 opens on the long-form messenger formula after a therefore-particle (oshb:Ezek.24.9). What its far face carries: MEASURED from the section-mark record, MT 24:8 is followed by a PE (petuchah, open section, single-witness) - and nothing else, because MEASURED from the pointed Hebrew witness MT 24:8 ends on a purpose infinitive (oshb:Ezek.24.8), with no utterance, recognition or I-YHWH-have-spoken signature anywhere in that verse. Whether CUT-RULE licenses it: it does NOT. Limb (a) fails, because the addressee does not change - MT 24:6 already addresses the bloody city (oshb:Ezek.24.6) and MT 24:9 addresses that same city. Limb (b) fails, because the verse immediately before it does not END on a close-role formula, and a mark alone never satisfies limb (b). The stated ground on which this row holds: a licensed text signal outranking a section mark the PE after MT 24:8 is weak corroboration and is disclosed FOR the alternative it corroborates, not for this row, and it is outranked by the licensed drivers this row does rest on - the fused dateline-plus-word-event onset at 24:1 and the stacked I-YHWH-have-spoken plus utterance close at 24:14. unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:20 opens with the strict word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.28.20). 28:21 supplies set-your-face plus the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל צִיד֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עָלֶֽיהָ" (oshb:Ezek.28.21) — "toward Sidon". In the WEB, “Son of man, set your face toward Sidon, and prophesy against it,” (web:Ezek.28.21). The verdict carries two 3mp recognition clauses in sequence: 28:22 ("וְאָמַרְתָּ֗ כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֤י עָלַ֨יִךְ֙ צִיד֔וֹן וְנִכְבַּדְתִּ֖י בְּתוֹכֵ֑ךְ וְֽיָדְע֞וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה בַּעֲשׂ֥וֹתִי בָ֛הּ שְׁפָטִ֖ים וְנִקְדַּ֥שְׁתִּי בָֽהּ", oshb:Ezek.28.22) and 28:23 ("וְשִׁלַּחְתִּי בָ֞הּ דֶּ֤בֶר וָדָם֙ בְּח֣וּצוֹתֶ֔יהָ וְנִפְלַ֤ל חָלָל֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ בְּחֶ֥רֶב עָלֶ֖יהָ מִסָּבִ֑יב וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה", oshb:Ezek.28.23); both are disclosed as internal, paragraph-final refrains rather than the row's close, since no fresh onset device separates them from what follows (28:22-24 read as one continuous accusation-then-plague verdict against the same addressee). Close (both sides): 28:24 ends "וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל סִלּ֤וֹן מַמְאִיר֙ וְק֣וֹץ מַכְאִ֔ב מִכֹּל֙ סְבִ֣יבֹתָ֔ם הַשָּׁאטִ֖ים אוֹתָ֑ם וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.28.24), pivoting from Sidon (2fs) to "the house of Israel" (3mp) while itself closing on an Adonai-form recognition variant (sweep: 5 verses; "then they shall know that I am the Lord YHWH"), with a SAMEKH immediately after — this SAMEKH is the Masoretic paragraph's own mark, confirming the row's close rather than diverging from it. Behind this row, 28:19 closed the king-of-Tyre qinah on parashah evidence alone; ahead, 28:25 opens a fresh messenger formula for the Israel-gathering promise.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 28:23/28:24 instead (ending the row on the strict 3mp recognition inside 28:23 and opening a fresh row at 28:24) is the strongest rejected alternative: 28:23 does close its own recognition clause, but 28:24's SAMEKH is the Masoretic paragraph's own mark and 28:24 itself opens the addressee-class shift toward Israel that the messenger formula at 28:25 completes, so the SAMEKH-marked cut is taken here instead.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: 28:22 and 28:23 are disclosed as paragraph-final refrains, not row-final, because 28:24 continues the same verdict before the addressee shifts. No K/Q, editorial note, or paseq site falls inside 28:20-24 itself; the chapter's two paseq sites stand at Ezek.28.2 and Ezek.28.25, outside this span.

unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: Ezek.44.5 opens with a son-of-man address launching an instructional mode; 44.6 and 44.9 both carry the messenger formula, addressed throughout to the same topic (the house of Israel's abominations in admitting uncircumcised foreigners to the sanctuary) with no addressee-class change between them, so neither reopens the row on its own. The unit turns at 44.10 to the Levites' judgment for their prior idolatry: they may minister but may not approach as priests, with the utterance signature appearing mid-paragraph at 44.12 (paragraph-final, not row-final, since no fresh onset follows immediately) and the paragraph closing at 44.14. Close: the pe parashah mark recorded after Ezek.44.14 corroborates that close; the very next verse, 44.15, turns to a different priestly class (the sons of Zadok) with its own utterance signature near its opening -- an addressee-class shift inside the same law section.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 44.9/44.10 (foreigner law versus the Levites' judgment), since 44.9 is itself a messenger-formula restatement. Rejected because no addressee-class change occurs there -- both halves concern the same reform of sanctuary access -- and no parashah or refrain marks that point, while 44.14's pe does mark a real close.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: The utterance signature at Ezek.44.12 is disclosed as a mid-paragraph close, not row-final, since mid-unit occurrences are paragraph-final unless a fresh onset follows (none does before 44.14). The pe recorded after Ezek.44.14 is disclosed single-witness. strongest_rejected_alternative.before: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. Weighed under A9/A16 and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it stands in the division plan's closed 20-verse transport list, so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. unchanged_prose_now.boundary_rationale: Onset: no formula device opens Ezek.48.8; the seam behind it at 48.7/48.8 is argued from the northern block's own close (the 'one portion' refrain at 48.7) and a change of listed object -- from tribal portions to the holy offering itself. The row covers the dimensions of the holy portion given to the sanctuary, priests and Levites (8-14), the remaining strip for the city and its common land (15-19), the whole square portion set apart with the sanctuary at its centre (20), and the prince's land on either side of the holy portion and the city, framed by Judah's and Benjamin's borders (21-22). A samekh mark is recorded after Ezek.48.11, mid-unit, inside the priests' portion; disclosed, but it does not cut, since it is unaccompanied by any change of addressee or genre and the holy-portion description continues without a fresh onset. A paseq is recorded within Ezek.48.22 (count-only, single-witness). Close: the next verse, 48.23, reopens the tribal-portion list on its own resumption formula, a change of listed object back from the holy portion, city and prince to the southern tribes -- a real content seam at the list's internal division, formula-free like this row's own onset.
unchanged_prose_now.strongest_rejected_alternative: The single 48.1-29 row treating the holy portion, city and prince's land as one continuation of the tribal-portion list with no internal seam. Rejected because 48.8 turns on its own change of listed object (from tribal portions to the holy offering), and cutting there discloses a real, though formula-free, content division rather than folding three distinct topics -- tribal portions, sanctuary land, and city/prince land -- into a single 29-verse row.
unchanged_prose_now.device_notes: Neither this row's onset at 48.8 nor its close before 48.23 carries a formula device; both are argued from a change of listed object, disclosed as such. The samekh recorded after Ezek.48.11 is single-witness, mid-unit, non-cutting. Held at medium_low.
